web.description:
**2026 Hospital Patient Flow Management Summit**

Today the nation’s healthcare environment has recognized that enhanced and efficient hospital-wide patient flow is essential in achieving value based health and delivering safe, high-quality patient centric healthcare. Such strategies are improving hospital-wide patient throughput to reduce wait times, re-design care management, and move the patient smoothly and efficiently from admission to discharge. Enhanced patient flow results in appropriate high-quality healthcare, improved patient satisfaction, and increased hospital profitability.

We have created a high-level forum featuring knowledgeable leaders and executives from hospitals and health systems who will share their perspectives, valuable insights and expertise on how to be best equipped for the rapidly evolving landscape of Patient Flow Management. Attendees will benefit from learning about best practices and strategies that have been deployed to address the challenges presented under the current healthcare environment impacting hospitals and health systems in effectively managing patient flow.

By attending the **2026 Hospital Patient Flow Management Summit**, you will learn what others in the Patient Flow Management and Emergency Medicine arenas are doing to be prepared for the challenges that lie ahead in 2027!

Business Research Intelligence Network’s Patient Flow Management Summit brings together hospital operations leaders, emergency department leaders and capacity management teams addressing the mounting pressures of overcrowding, boarding and throughput bottlenecks.

Agenda

[Day One – Thursday, January 28, 2027](https://brinetwork.com/2027-annual-patient-flow-management-summit/#collapse-6a7dfc96a97c8d797a68)

**8:15am – 9:00am** **Whole-System Patient Flow: Moving Beyond Department-Level Fixes** Most patient flow research concentrates on individual units or emergency departments but breakthrough improvements require whole-hospital perspectives coordinating capacity across all units simultaneously. Organizations achieving transformative results recognize patient flow as interconnected system requiring alignment from admission through discharge across multiple departments, specialties and support services.

**Candace Kravetz, MSN, RN, CMS-RN, NE-BC** _Manager Clinical Administrators/Capacity & Transfer Management Center_ **WakeMed Health and Hospitals**

**Marcy van Schagen, MSN, RN, CNML** _Director System Capacity and Patient Placement_ **WakeMed Health and Hospitals**

**Carissa J.**

**10:15am – 11:00am** **End-to-End Patient Flow: Integrating Transfer Center, Command Center, Care Management, Discharge and Bed Management** Optimizing patient flow requires more than improving a single-entry point, bed board or discharge process. High-performing organizations are connecting transfer center intake, command center situational awareness, care management barrier removal, discharge readiness planning and bed management into one coordinated operating model that manages the full patient journey from referral or admission request through safe transition out of the hospital.

**Brooke Gentzler, MS, CNMT** Administrator, Rochester Hospital Operations Command Center

**11:00am – 11:45am** **GE**

System-wide flow strategies enable load balancing by sending appropriate patients to facilities with capacity, standardized protocols ensuring consistent quality regardless of location and centralized command centers orchestrating system-level capacity.

**Dr.** **Joshua Martin, RN, BSN, MHA, DBA, NE-BC** _Director of Nursing_ **Pioneers Medical Center**

**Jeffrey S.** **Kuo, MD, MMM, FACEP, FAAEM** _System Chair, Patient Flow & EMS_ _System Medical Director, Emergency Management & Security_ _System Medical Director, Emergency Medicine Telehealth_ _Physician Lead, Event Medicine_ _Senior Staff Emergency Medicine Physician_ _Emergency Response & Airway Management Physician, New Orleans Saints_ **Ochsner Health**

**Amber Hebert** _Assistant Vice President Patient Flow_ **Ochsner Health**

Leaders successfully building flow-focused cultures share approaches to stakeholder engagement, resistance management, creating visibility into how individual roles affect overall flow and celebrating improvements.

Panelists:

[Day Two – Friday, January 29, 2027](https://brinetwork.com/2027-annual-patient-flow-management-summit/#collapse-028edb66a97c8d797f86)

Limited subspecialty resources, highly variable patient acuity, family-centered care, and expansive regional transport networks require a unique approach to patient flow and capacity management.

**Rey Garcia, MSN, RN, CCRN** _Director, Driscoll Access Center_ **Driscoll Children's Hospital**

**Kirby Garcia** _Manager, Driscoll Access Center_ **Driscoll Children's Hospital**

MD Anderson's redesigned Ambulatory Clinical Care Center, combined with a Clinical Decision Unit for observation and treatment, demonstrates how clinical and operational innovation can reshape patient flow.

**Kathleen Denton, PhD, CPHQ, SSBB, CPXP** _Director, Office of Patient Experience_ **MD Anderson Cancer Center**

**10:15am – 11:00am** **Patient Flow as Patient Safety Imperative** Flow breakdowns directly cause patient harm through crowded emergency departments increasing clinical risk, prolonged stays exposing patients to hospital-acquired conditions, poorly coordinated transfers creating care gaps and fragmented transitions missing deterioration opportunities.

**Lorelei Stellwag, DNP, RN, NE-BC** _Vice President_ _MedStar Capacity and Transfer Center_ **MedStar Health**

**Diana Pancu, MD** _Chief MedStar Triage Officer and Physician Director, MedStar Capacity and Transfer Center_

_Director of Quality Assurance and Education, Emergency Medicine, MedStar Franklin Square Medical Center_ **MedStar Health**

**Gregory Marchand, M.D.**

_Physician Director_

**MedStar Health**

We’ll explore evidence-based ED throughput strategies including split-flow models separating high and low acuity patients, fast-track systems, provider-in-triage approaches and observation unit expansion.

In this engaging session, attendees will learn how overcrowding, ED boarding, discharge delays, and capacity constraints directly impact the patient experience—and why improving flow is one of the most powerful strategies for improving satisfaction, safety, and trust. Attendees will leave with actionable insights to improve throughput while delivering a more seamless, compassionate experience for patients and families.

**Paul S.**

**12:30pm**

**Conference Concludes**

# A Comprehensive Approach to Patient Flow: Analytics, Capacity Command Center, and Discharge Lounge
## Abstract
UCSF Health opened its Patient Capacity Management Center in 2023.

## Full Content
UCSF Health, which cares for patients across Northern California and internationally, has spent the last two years revamping its approach to patient flow.

### Better collaboration relies on common understanding
UCSF Health formed a group of capacity management stakeholders to identify bottlenecks and workflow inconsistencies and to provide staff a deeper insight into each other’s contributions to patient flow.

### Creating a central space for capacity management
The PCMC brought together staff from across disciplines to monitor throughput and capacity management for its three adult hospitals and, more recently, for its pediatric and women’s health hospitals and two community hospitals.

These meetings help them prioritize patient placement across their hospitals and anticipate UCSF Health’s bed needs by level of acuity.

### Looking ahead
This expansion is supported by the newly centralized approach to managing patient throughput and capacity and tailoring solutions to meet the specific needs of each of these diverse hospitals.
